title: Elenia’s Exile · The Door Left Open
dek: Elenia’s return of the fallen and her duel with Magnus divide her friends and Zarathis. Bowene hears them, orders her departure, and offers a sending stone, aid and a path to Babel without promising an unconditional return.

facts.Setting: Below Ciaránach; departure from the Shining Shores

facts.Outcome: Elenia must leave; companions join her, with aid and continued contact offered

body:
When Bowene returned from Ciaránach, he had to judge an act that had brought families home and shaken the rules by which his people lived. Elenia’s divine aid had returned soldiers to life. Her victory over Magnus in the Crucible had then left even some of her friends horrified.

On 22 December 2025, he let them speak before the verdict. Olokun and Aravil defended Elenia, Adelia and Magnus supported banishment, and Elenia admitted a responsibility the argument could not place entirely on her god. The decision sent her away, but preserved a possibility of talking and working together again.

The dead who came home

The judgment followed a memorial that had become a public crisis. Elenia had opened a box before the mourners, saying that a friend had helped her return lives stolen by Death. Flames became flesh, and 99 soldiers appeared, frightened and bewildered. Some in the crowd celebrated. Others condemned what they had seen.

The dispute became a sanctioned Crucible of Valor between Elenia and Magnus. Bowene declared it fair and willing, a fight to the death for their convictions, while reserving the possibility of further judgment. Elenia won with a display that visibly called on divine power and terribly altered Magnus’s face. He fell dead; after she released her magic and healing was given, he emerged alive. No named resurrection spell is established by that sequence.

The witnesses could not agree on what the victory proved. Gartina defended the rules of the contest; Adelia condemned the force Elenia used. Draygar urged mercy, and Bowene was left speechless. At the later hearing, Elenia would clarify an important limit: the returned soldiers were those lost to Aionia. Those taken by Death had not been recovered.

A judgment after mourning

Bowene had praised Aria at her funeral. By the time he returned from Ciaránach to judge Elenia, he was also reconsidering what her life and leadership had left behind. He came down alone, without a retinue or banners, carrying the weight of a decision that would divide people he wanted to keep together.

He acknowledged the families reunited through Elenia, then the horror of the divine power used against Magnus. Though the duel had been honorably sanctioned, he could not put the sight out of his mind. He invited the outsiders to speak before he passed judgment. Elenia stopped to listen, anxious to know her fate.

She said she had not wanted to break their ways and had hoped they might accept returns from a death caused by an immortal. Then she took responsibility for the harm to Magnus: Hope had not wanted his face taken. That had been her own choice, and she might not have reversed it without Hope’s protest.

She would try to follow the judgment. Her own wish for Zarathis was a return to mortal work: great buildings, towers, statues and intricate gardens. The cosmic war, she argued, had cost lives and Aria herself while leaving them enemies of both sides.

The friends who took different sides

Olokun stood with her. He described the outsiders’ fight against Death and the aid Hope had given them. He defended the return of the lost as a gift to the land’s families, not a demand for payment or obedience. If Bowene sent Elenia away, he said, he should send him too. Elenia corrected his account of whose dead had actually returned; his loyalty did not remove the need to get that history right.

Aravil challenged the judgment through Zarathis’s own standards. If might proved worth, how could the authorities dismiss both Elenia’s return of the soldiers and her victory in their own Crucible? She called the unseen authorities into question and demanded to know whether tradition mattered more than the strength they claimed to honor.

Adelia spoke against her friend. She agreed with part of what her friend had wanted, but said the return should have been discussed first. She condemned the divine violence against Magnus as an attempted murder and said it had damaged her trust. She asked whether Elenia could still be trusted.

Magnus spoke for the traditions he had defended and promised to abide by Bowene’s decision. Asked plainly where they stood, Olokun and Aravil declared solidarity with Elenia. Adelia moved beside Magnus. Bowene required an answer in words as well as the gesture, and she said she supported banishment. Magnus confirmed the same. Adelia was crying as she did so.

Who must leave

Bowene answered each position. Nobody could deny what Olokun had done for the land, he said, but the outsiders also needed to understand a history larger than their own lives. He described Zarathian independence as a defense against the gods’ betrayal. To Aravil, he answered that divine assistance was not the same as mortal strength; dependence on a power beyond themselves was precisely what their customs resisted.

He also admitted that those customs might need to change. He said the Golden Ones agreed that change was possible, but insisted that their people must make it. Elenia’s wonders and Olokun’s service had not made the dispute disappear, and simply setting aside the law would not settle it.

But Elenia must be exiled. We shall not banishHigh Lord Bowene

The departure was required for Elenia. Bowene named Aravil and Olokun with her, in keeping with the solidarity they had offered, and asked who else wished to join them. Their acceptance did not turn every companion into someone convicted of the same offense. Those who remained were asked to work in good faith with the people of the land.

Aravil was surprised by the compromise. She accepted the offer to go where the fight against Death was fiercer. Olokun accepted too, and told Bowene to call if the people of Fein Uaill needed him again.

Help for the next struggle

Bowene proposed Babel-Ashur, a land the Zarathian mages had found while scouting for the battle that ended with Aria’s death. It was ruled by Babelomnys, a Knight of Death. The company could continue its own war there. He said they knew Gartina had a tuning fork for the journey.

He offered the intelligence they had gathered and supplies for the fight. He also gave Elenia a sending stone. That small object changed her response: she brightened and immediately asked who would hold the other end. She hoped for a connection to Arandiel too, so she could answer if her people needed protection. Bowene said that could be arranged.

These were offers of aid across a separation he was still imposing. They did not make the order voluntary, supply a fixed term for it, or show that all distrust had ended. They did give the departing company a destination, material help and an intended way to keep talking. No final keeper for the other sending-stone connection was named before they began preparing to leave.

The possibility of return

Bowene distinguished exile from a door permanently shut. He acknowledged, after contemplation, that Aria had not been perfect. He would work with the companions who stayed to pursue changes in law, strength and justice. Perhaps that would one day make coexistence possible.

He did not give Elenia an automatic right to return or announce that the laws had already changed. Nor did the judgment establish an exclusion from every shore in the world. The opening was specific and conditional: continued work might let these people share Fein Uaill again.

The court’s response was mixed. When the crowd dispersed, the narrator records many finding the compromise wise, while some radicals and fundamentalists remained upset. Arandiel began moving toward the Shining Shores. Bowene took Magnus aside for the private audience he had requested. The contents of that conversation are not supplied by this public scene.

A departure with an aftermath

The travelers were to meet at the Shining Shores within an hour and leave at sunset, with an escort. Olokun joked that this left no time to choose his best clothes. Bowene offered people to help pack. When Olokun explained the joke, Bowene admitted that the decision weighed too heavily on him to hear humor easily. Olokun urged him to care for his people and promised that humor would return.

Elenia and the others began naming possible companions. Wren seemed likely to come; Krone, Draygar, Gartina, Arjahn, Eugene, Dale and Saray were discussed. Olokun suggested a trail of Gartina’s steak to draw the two brothers after them. These were invitations and guesses, not a confirmed final passenger list.

Adelia offered future help if Elenia sent for her. Elenia turned instead to Olokun and Aravil. Adelia pulled away from Magnus’s attempt to comfort her and later said she felt she had lost a best friend. His suggestion that she could now join the Silver Star did not answer the grief: the order was far from her mind. A legal compromise had not repaired the friendship.

The exiles were sent away. Their next struggle would be keeping a foothold in Babel-Ashur. Later accounts of peace and reconciliation in Fein Uaill remain alongside distrust and efforts to gain influence; they do not annul this judgment. For now, Elenia had to leave, companions chose to go with her, and Bowene deliberately kept a channel of contact open.
